title: Test Engineer
summary: Join the production team to test electronic assemblies and spacecraft systems, analyse results and write test reports, working with Design Engineers to debug new and existing designs.
responsibilities: Support spacecraft assembly and deliver hardware to standard, budget and schedule
Align test schedules with the Project Manager and project reviews
Support Design Engineers in testing and debugging current and new designs
Verify spacecraft hardware meets customer requirements
Write test reports with recommended actions, within the Quality Management System
required: Relevant degree or equivalent work experience
Electrical and electronic engineering principles
Reading schematics and PCB layouts to debug hardware
Battery packs, power systems, DC-DC converters
Working knowledge of test equipment
Following and writing test and evaluation plans
Health and Safety and Quality Management Systems awareness
Clear documentation and English communication
desired: Python or C++ for test automation
notes: Fully on site. A Basic Disclosure check may be required.

title: Embedded Software Engineer
summary: Own the architecture, design and implementation of embedded software and firmware for small satellites and subsystems, from drivers to encrypted communications, and improve the embedded SDLC.
responsibilities: Architect, design and implement embedded software and firmware for new products
Improve the embedded SDLC: CI, automated testing, release management
Mentor and code-review other engineers
Lead integration, verification and validation of complex embedded systems
Resolve the hardest hardware/software integration issues with deep debugging
required: Embedded software experience in space or another mission or safety-critical domain
Deep C for resource-constrained real-time systems
RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr) or embedded Linux kernel and drivers
ARM Cortex-M/R/A or RISC-V, SPI, I2C, UART, ADC
Reading schematics and datasheets; oscilloscopes, logic analysers, debuggers
Git, CI/CD and automated testing
Linux command line and GNU toolchain
notes: Hybrid possible. A Basic Disclosure check may be required.

title: Principal Electronics Engineer
summary: Technical authority in the Electronics team: drive definition, development, verification and qualification of spacecraft electronics and electrical architectures, and mentor the team.
responsibilities: Act as technical authority for spacecraft electronics and electrical architecture
Lead senior design reviews, investigations, NCRs, ECNs and risk assessments
Advise on EMC, signal and power integrity, grounding, reliability, DFX
Support the Electronics Team Leader on risk, estimates and approach
Mentor engineers and improve design quality
required: Significant analogue/digital hardware design in high-reliability regulated environments
Design, verification, qualification and production release
EMC, reliability, manufacturability, testability, fault investigation
Spacecraft electrical interfaces: power, RF, digital, analogue, harnessing
CAN, SPI, I2C, UART, ADCs, DC/DC converters, LDOs
Reviewing schematics, PCB layouts, release packs, NCRs and ECNs
Mentoring and cross-functional technical leadership
desired: Power, battery, RF, OBC or mixed-signal specialism
notes: Senior hire. A Basic Disclosure check may be required.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
summary: Technical Lead for spacecraft projects: own architecture, requirements, interfaces, budgets and verification across disciplines, and act as the key technical interface with customers.
responsibilities: Act as Technical Lead for spacecraft projects or major work packages
Define spacecraft and mission architectures, CONOPS and product breakdown
Lead requirements definition, traceability and verification
Lead interface management and ICDs; own mass, power, data, delta-V and link budgets
Plan V&V and support AIT; resolve test anomalies
Mission and constellation analysis in STK or equivalent
Lead technical input to bids; mentor engineers
required: Significant systems engineering on complex multidisciplinary systems
Owned a subsystem or major work package through to verification
Proven multidisciplinary technical leadership
Architecture integrating hardware, software, payload, ground and operations
Requirements management, traceability and compliance
ICD ownership and spacecraft system budgets
V&V, spacecraft test planning and AIT support
Excellent stakeholder communication

title: Satellite Operations Engineer
summary: Operate the group's in-orbit fleet, including the Sedna maritime constellation and VIREON-1, from LEOP through routine operations: pass planning, commanding, telemetry analysis and anomaly response.
responsibilities: Plan and run ground station passes and command schedules
Monitor spacecraft health telemetry and trend subsystem performance
Lead anomaly investigations with the engineering teams
Support LEOP and commissioning of new satellites
Write and maintain flight procedures and automate routine operations
required: Degree in aerospace, electronics, physics or similar
Hands-on spacecraft operations or mission control experience
Understanding of LEO orbits, ADCS, power and comms subsystems
Telemetry and telecommand concepts (CCSDS or similar)
Python scripting for automation and analysis
Willingness to join an on-call rota
desired: Ground station networks (KSAT, AWS Ground Station, Leaf Space)
Flight dynamics tools such as STK or GMAT
notes: Inferred from the Satellite Operations Engineer employee spotlight and the growing in-orbit fleet.

title: RF / Microwave Engineer
summary: Design and verify microwave and millimetre-wave receivers for radiometer instruments on satellite and airborne platforms, from component design to space qualification in the in-house lab.
responsibilities: Design LNAs, mixers, filters and receiver chains for radiometers
Simulate and lay out RF circuits and waveguide components
Characterise hardware with VNAs, spectrum analysers and noise figure meters
Support space qualification and environmental testing
Document designs to ESA project standards
required: MSc in microwave engineering, electronics or physics
Microwave or mm-wave circuit design experience
Keysight ADS, CST or HFSS
Lab measurement: VNA, noise figure, spectrum analysis
Fluent English
notes: Inferred from AAC Omnisys' radiometer and SKA feed system work and the Technical Project Manager listing asking for microwave backgrounds.

title: Mechanical Engineer, Spacecraft Structures
summary: Design and analyse structures and mechanisms for EPIC small satellite platforms and payload accommodation, through to vibration and thermal-vacuum qualification.
responsibilities: Design primary and secondary structures, brackets and enclosures
Run structural FEA (modal, random vibration, quasi-static) and thermal analysis
Produce drawings with GD&T and manage suppliers for machined parts
Support integration, vibration and TVAC campaigns
Maintain mass budgets and mechanical ICDs
required: Degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering
3D CAD (SolidWorks, Creo or NX)
Structural FEA (Ansys, Nastran or Abaqus)
Design for manufacture and GD&T
Hands-on integration or test experience
notes: Inferred from the Senior Mechanical Engineer spotlight and platform growth.

title: ADCS / GNC Engineer
summary: Develop attitude determination and control algorithms and support integrated ADCS products for small satellites, from simulation to flight software and on-orbit tuning.
responsibilities: Design attitude determination and control algorithms (Kalman filters, pointing control)
Build and maintain MATLAB/Simulink or Python simulation environments
Port algorithms to embedded C and verify with hardware-in-the-loop
Calibrate sensors: star trackers, gyros, magnetometers, sun sensors
Support commissioning and in-orbit anomaly analysis
required: MSc in aerospace engineering, control or similar
Attitude dynamics and control theory
Kalman filtering and sensor fusion
MATLAB/Simulink or Python simulation
C or C++ for embedded deployment
notes: Inferred from AAC Hyperion's ADCS product line.

title: Ground Segment Software Engineer
summary: Build the ground and data platform behind Space Data as a Service: mission control software, ground station integration and the pipelines that turn downlinked data into customer products.
responsibilities: Develop mission control and scheduling services
Integrate commercial ground station networks and APIs
Build data ingestion and processing pipelines for maritime and EO products
Run services on cloud infrastructure with CI/CD and monitoring
Work with operations and data teams on tooling
required: Professional Python or Go backend development
Distributed systems, queues and databases
Cloud (AWS, GCP or Azure), containers and infrastructure as code
Testing, CI/CD and observability
Good English communication
notes: Inferred from the Data and Services division, Sedna and VIREON-1 data products.

title: FPGA Engineer, Onboard Data Processing
summary: Design FPGA firmware for payload data handling and onboard processing of Earth observation imagery, working with Spacemetric's Bluestone onboard software.
responsibilities: Develop VHDL or Verilog for payload interfaces and data handling
Implement image processing and compression pipelines on SoC FPGAs
Write testbenches and run hardware verification
Integrate with embedded Linux on Zynq-class devices
Address radiation effects with mitigation such as TMR and scrubbing
required: MSc in electronics or computer engineering
VHDL or Verilog with Vivado or Libero
Simulation and verification (testbenches, UVM or cocotb)
High-speed interfaces (SpaceWire, LVDS, Ethernet)
Bring-up and lab debugging
notes: Inferred from the Spacemetric acquisition and VIREON-1 EO payload.
